questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Understanding Markets' refers to.
questions.a: A market is any arrangement where buyers and sellers meet to exchange goods and services at agreed prices; Adam Smith saw prosperity flow from markets, since people can obtain what they cannot make themselves.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Understanding Markets'.
questions.a: Markets turn strangers into partners: price and exchange let each person's skill serve everyone.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Understanding Markets' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Many Kinds of Markets' refers to.
questions.a: Markets come in many shapes: weekly haats, neighbourhood kirana shops, malls, online platforms, and wholesale mandis; each differs in scale, goods and the distance between producer and buyer.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Many Kinds of Markets'.
questions.a: Same work, many forms: every kind of market matches buyers and sellers in its own way.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Many Kinds of Markets' taught, and from which source text?

Explain in your own words what 'The Chain of Markets' refers to.
questions.a: Goods travel through a chain of markets: the producer sells to a wholesaler, the wholesaler to retailers, and retailers to consumers, each link adding transport, storage and a margin to the price.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Chain of Markets'.
questions.a: Every hand in the chain earns and adds cost: knowing the chain explains why prices differ from farm-gate rates.

Explain in your own words what 'Being a Smart Consumer' refers to.
questions.a: Buyers must stay alert: check labels, dates and quality marks, compare prices, and use the BEE star ratings on electronic devices to weigh running cost, not just the sticker price.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Being a Smart Consumer'.
questions.a: An informed buyer disciplines the market: careful comparison rewards fair sellers and squeezes out poor goods.
